items.title: NEA working on winter power management
items.blurb: Officials say there won’t be load-shedding this winter despite flood damage to hydropower infrastructure along Trishuli corridor.

items.title: BP Highway to close at night in Kavrepalanchok from September 24 to 28 amid flood risk
items.blurb: Authorities will stop vehicles from using the highway from 5 pm to 5 am, while the weather office has urged people to postpone long-distance travel from September 25 to 27.

items.title: Kali Gandaki river settlements face rising flood risk
items.blurb: Around a dozen settlements along the river are exposed to sudden flooding, while authorities assess the threat from landslides and glacial hazards.

items.title: Death toll from capsized ship in Indonesia rises to 26 as search continues for 109 missing passengers
items.blurb: Divers managed to break the windows of the cabins on Tuesday but could not enter due to murky water and strong currents, making it impossible to retrieve bodies that had already been spotted.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods prompt ADB to cut Nepal’s growth forecast to 4.1 percent
items.blurb: The Asian Development Bank has raised its inflation forecast to 5.3 percent and expects the fiscal deficit to widen as reconstruction spending increases following the devastation.

items.title: Helicopters put on standby as heavy rain forecast
items.blurb: The Air Service Operators Association has directed its member companies to remain ready for possible rescue operations as heavy rain is forecast across Nepal from Thursday.

items.title: What kind of international environment is China trying to build?
items.blurb: Nepal-China relations can advance simultaneously across development, connectivity, technology, trade, tourism, education, disaster management, multilateral diplomacy, and global governance.

items.title: Hydropower producers seek changes to proposed IPO rules
items.blurb: Producers say the proposed eligibility framework does not reflect the financing needs and development cycle of hydropower projects.

items.title: Over 800 people remain missing from hydropower projects after Bhotekoshi floods, says energy minister Shrestha
items.blurb: Shrestha tells Parliament that search and rescue teams are still looking for workers believed to be trapped in underground structures or swept away by the August 26 disaster.

items.title: Guterres recalls Nepal glacier warning as climate risks grow
items.blurb: The UN chief said the impacts of climate change are arriving sooner and hitting harder, calling for more adaptation finance and a stronger Loss and Damage Fund as Nepal seeks international support after the August…

items.title: Flood destroys equipment, pushing back Siddhababa tunnel opening
items.blurb: Replacement electromechanical equipment must be brought through the Korala border, delaying the planned start of traffic by at least a month.

items.title: Khanal holds multiple diplomatic meetings in New York as Nepal establishes ties with Grenada
items.blurb: The foreign minister discusses flood recovery, development cooperation and stronger economic ties with his Indian counterpart, US officials and other foreign ministers during the UN General Assembly sidelines.

items.title: US announces additional $31 million support for Nepal’s flood recovery
items.blurb: The package includes funding for permanent bridges, humanitarian assistance and US-made drones, taking Washington’s total flood response and recovery support to more than $36 million.

items.title: What it means to be a peripheral country in the age of uncertainties
items.blurb: The government tricks the public into feeling that it is steering a steady ship, while structural policy, economic reality and disaster response crumble underneath.

items.title: For Bhotekoshi flood survivors, the tuin is an ordeal
items.blurb: In Nuwakot, locals walk for five to six hours to reach the tuin, an improvised cable crossing, then wait for another four to five hours to cross.
